workarounds.symptom: [Bug] ctx.debug/info/warning/error raise RuntimeError in background tasks (session is not available)
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(context): allow background task logging without a session. Target files: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/context.py, tests/server/test_context.py. - allow `Context.log()` to resolve the background task's captured session key when no live MCP session exists - keep server-side logging and skip only the unavailable client notification back-channel - add a regression test for `ctx.info()` in a worker context (Ref: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/5806)

workarounds.symptom: AssertionError: Unexpected message while using middleware
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Stop the SSE endpoint sending a second response after its stream. Target files: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/http.py, tests/server/http/test_http_middleware.py. an SSE app behind any `BaseHTTPMiddleware` logged `AssertionError: Unexpected message: {'type': 'http.response.start', ...}` every time a client disconnected. the unauthenticated `/sse` route was a request/response endpoint, so once `connect_sse` had streamed the whole response, Starlette sent the trailing empty `Response()` as a second `http.response.start`. the au... (Ref: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/6431)

workarounds.symptom: `StdioTransport(keep_alive=True)` can't be reused across concurrently-alive event loops — `initialize` handshake hangs for the full `init_timeout`
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Reconnect StdioTransport when reused on a different event loop. Target files: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/client/transports/stdio.py, tests/client/test_stdio.py, docs/clients/transports.mdx. a kept-alive stdio session belongs to the event loop that created it. reusing the same `Client` from a second loop handed that loop the first loop's session. its responses never arrived, so `async with client` hung forever, and `init_timeout` didn't bound it. (Ref: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/6425)

workarounds.symptom: `logging/setLevel` is ignored for `ctx.log()` calls from tools of a mounted server
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Apply logging/setLevel to mounted servers over HTTP sessions. Target files: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/context.py, fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/mixins/mcp_operations.py, fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/server.py. A handshake-era client that sent `logging/setLevel` over a stateful HTTP session still got sub-threshold `ctx.log()` messages from tools on mounted servers. The parent handled the request and saved the level in its own `_client_log_levels` dict, keyed by session id. The mounted tool's `Context` checked the child serve... (Ref: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/6421)

workarounds.symptom: A tool re-versioned with ToolTransformConfig(version=...) can't be called by its new version
workarounds.workaround: Fix: Call a re-versioned tool by its transformed version. Target files: fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/server/transforms/tool_transform.py, tests/server/test_tool_transformation.py. `ToolTransformConfig(version="2.0")` lists a tool under 2.0, but `call_tool(..., version="2.0")` failed with `Unknown tool`. The original version, which is no longer listed, still worked. `ToolTransform.get_tool` sent the caller's version spec unchanged to the source lookup, so the spec was checked against the source version and not the one the tool is listed... (Ref: https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/pull/6419)
